topics.title: Drones could deliver defibrillators faster
topics.summary: A new study suggests drone bases could help get defibrillators closer to people having cardiac arrests outside hospitals, especially where fixed devices are sparse.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a flying defibrillator buzzed into the neighborhood, who would be impressed, who would be suspicious, and who would immediately name it?

topics.title: Casino Secrets leak exposes gambling firms
topics.summary: A large leak of files from Curacao's gambling regulator is shedding light on offshore online casino ownership, licensing, and alleged targeting of customers in restricted markets.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a secretive industry gets mapped out in public, who studies the paperwork and who asks how nobody noticed sooner?

topics.title: Meta loses New Mexico privacy verdict
topics.summary: A New Mexico jury found Meta misled residents about Facebook data practices in a case tied to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Meta said it disagrees with the verdict.
topics.discussionPrompt: If an old privacy scandal is still producing new courtroom twists, who says accountability takes time and who says tech moves too fast for lawsuits?

topics.title: South Africa keeps door open to U.S. talks
topics.summary: South Africa's foreign minister said the country remains open to talks with the United States after visa restrictions and disagreements over investment and ownership rules.
topics.discussionPrompt: When diplomacy gets tense but everyone says talks can continue, who believes in patience and who wants a very clear agenda first?

topics.title: Climate Week weighs AI's energy appetite
topics.summary: Climate Week discussions in New York highlighted optimism around clean energy growth while raising concerns that data centers and AI could increase power and water demand.
topics.discussionPrompt: If AI can help solve climate problems while using a mountain of electricity, who calls it a tool and who calls it a tab?

topics.title: NASA previews deeper infrared telescope plans
topics.summary: NASA is teasing PRIMA, a proposed infrared space telescope meant to look deeper into dusty regions of the universe and build on discoveries from Webb.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a new telescope promises to see what older ones missed, who starts dreaming about alien planets and who asks about the budget?

topics.title: Japan runs room-temperature quantum computer
topics.summary: Researchers in Japan switched on the country's first full-stack room-temperature quantum computer and outlined ambitions to scale the system dramatically in future versions.
topics.discussionPrompt: If quantum computers get easier to run, who imagines breakthroughs and who quietly changes every password just in case?

topics.title: Study rewrites bats' origin story
topics.summary: A genetic study reported by The Guardian suggests bats may have originated in Europe, challenging earlier assumptions about the evolutionary history of the flying mammals.
topics.discussionPrompt: When a family tree gets redrawn millions of years later, who updates the textbook and who wants the ancestors to explain themselves?

topics.title: Wall Street steadies as oil cools
topics.summary: U.S. stocks rose toward the end of the week as oil prices eased, giving markets a break after recent swings tied to bond yields and energy worries.
topics.discussionPrompt: When markets calm down because oil prices take a breather, who relaxes and who waits for the next chart to misbehave?

topics.title: Smartphone-only fares frustrate school families
topics.summary: In England, families without smartphones may face higher school bus costs as some cheaper travel passes move into apps, raising access questions for students.
topics.discussionPrompt: If a discount only exists inside an app, who calls that convenient and who asks what happens to everyone without the gadget?
